lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Application or project: receiving and acting on feedback

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic receiving and acting on feedback task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner reads a sample piece of written feedback printed on this task sheet (a coach's comment after a scrimmage) and, without contacting the feedback-giver, writes a specific plan describing what they will change and how they'll check that the change worked.
safetyNotes: The feedback used in this lesson is a sample provided on the task sheet; the learner does not contact a real coach or teacher as part of this task.

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l04-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l04-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l04-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l04-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Explain why naming a specific, observable check for whether your change worked matters more than just deciding to 'try harder' or 'do better.'

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g9-u05-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Specificity of the identified behavior: Names the specific behavior the feedback points to and when it broke down, using the feedback's own details. | Concreteness of the response plan: Names one specific action and one specific, observable way to check whether it worked. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l04-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner draft a second response plan for a different sample piece of feedback (a teacher's comment such as 'Your thesis is unclear in the second paragraph') using the same specific-action-plus-specific-check structure, and compare how the check differs between an athletic skill and a writing skill.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic receiving and acting on feedback task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: paper or a document
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: receiving and acting on feedback worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner reads a sample piece of written feedback printed on this task sheet (a coach's comment after a scrimmage) and, without contacting the feedback-giver, writes a specific plan describing what they will change and how they'll check that the change worked.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact receiving and acting on feedback decision or action.

Model move 2: Read this feedback a coach left after a scrimmage: 'You had good instincts on defense, but you stopped calling out switches after the first quarter, and twice that led to an open shot for the other team.
Model move 3: Identify the specific, observable behavior the feedback wants changed, not just the general topic.

Model check: Specificity of the identified behavior: Names the specific behavior the feedback points to and when it broke down, using the feedback's own details. | Concreteness of the response plan: Names one specific action and one specific, observable way to check whether it worked.

resources.title: receiving and acting on feedback action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for receiving and acting on feedback.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: receiving and acting on feedback coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner reads a sample piece of written feedback printed on this task sheet (a coach's comment after a scrimmage) and, without contacting the feedback-giver, writes a specific plan describing what they will change and how they'll check that the change worked.

Coach direction: Read this feedback a coach left after a scrimmage: 'You had good instincts on defense, but you stopped calling out switches after the first quarter, and twice that led to an open shot for the other team.
Learner prompt: Separate this feedback into what it praises and what it asks the learner to change, quoting the exact phrase for each.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: receiving and acting on feedback complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Identify the specific, observable behavior the feedback wants changed, not just the general topic.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I named the specific behavior (calling out switches) rather than a vague label like 'communication.'
Response 2 (t2-p2): I identified when the behavior broke down (after the first quarter) as part of naming the problem.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: receiving and acting on feedback minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain why naming a specific, observable check for whether your change worked matters more than just deciding to 'try harder' or 'do better.'

Success checks: Specificity of the identified behavior: Names the specific behavior the feedback points to and when it broke down, using the feedback's own details. | Concreteness of the response plan: Names one specific action and one specific, observable way to check whether it worked.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: receiving and acting on feedback supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l04-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g9-u05-l04-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional receiving and acting on feedback condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Specificity of the identified behavior: Names the specific behavior the feedback points to and when it broke down, using the feedback's own details. | Concreteness of the response plan: Names one specific action and one specific, observable way to check whether it worked..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l04-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

coachMoves: Ask the learner to name the condition.

simulationRoute.title: receiving and acting on feedback — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: Complete the receiving and acting on feedback task using the fictional condition and invented, non-sensitive details on the delivered independent card.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

learnerEvidence: one revision when a step changed
evidence.reflectionPrompt: Explain why naming a specific, observable check for whether your change worked matters more than just deciding to 'try harder' or 'do better.'
observableCriteria: Specificity of the identified behavior: Names the specific behavior the feedback points to and when it broke down, using the feedback's own details.
Concreteness of the response plan: Names one specific action and one specific, observable way to check whether it worked.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g9-u05-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Specificity of the identified behavior: Names the specific behavior the feedback points to and when it broke down, using the feedback's own details. | Concreteness of the response plan: Names one specific action and one specific, observable way to check whether it worked.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l04-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
